summary: Page section header: eyebrow, title, description, and an end-aligned actions slot (tabs, filters, “see all”) that wraps below the text in narrow containers.
whenToUse: Opening the sections of a landing page or portal (events, articles, speakers).
Placing filters or a “see all” link next to the title.
whenNotToUse: Main page title (h1) with breadcrumbs: use Heading or the page header pattern.
Headings inside a card: use the card title.

props.name: actions
props.description: End slot: tabs, filters, links, or buttons.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level in the document structure.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size of the title, independent of the level.

props.name: titleId
props.description: Id of the title, used to label the enclosing <section aria-labelledby>. Generated if omitted.

inherits: HTML attributes of the <div> (id, style, data-*, aria-*).
accessibility: The title is a real heading (h2 by default): choose headingLevel based on the page structure.
The eyebrow precedes the title in reading order; don’t use it for essential information that isn’t also in the title.
Link the section to the title with <section aria-labelledby={titleId}> to create a named region.
responsive: Text and actions sit on the same row and wrap when there isn’t enough space (flex-wrap).
Below 640 px, md/lg titles drop to headline-sm.
customization: Tokens: --dc-color-text-link for the eyebrow, headline/title type scale.
commonMistakes: Using size to change the hierarchy: the level is set with headingLevel.
Putting too many actions in the slot: prefer one filter and one link.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: With filters
examples.description: Eyebrow, title, and a ToggleGroup at the end.

limits: Start alignment only; for centered headers use Heading and Text.
